item.title: The Normalization of Deviance in AI
item.description:
Author: wunderwuzzi
Date: December 04, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "AI Safety", "Security", "Organizational Culture", "Technology Risk"]
Summary:
  • The AI industry risks normalizing deviance like in the Challenger disaster.
  • Large language models (LLMs) are unreliable and require security controls.
  • Over-trusting LLM outputs leads to safety and security risks.
  • Adversarial attacks like prompt injection exploit these weaknesses.
  • Cultural drift causes risky shortcuts to become accepted norms.
  • This threatens AI system safety and user security.

item.title: Knowledge Weaving Jailbreak Tactic
item.description:
Date: December 01, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Large Language Models", "Adversarial Attacks", "Safety and Alignment", "Cybersecurity"]
Summary:
  • Large language models have a vulnerability in their safety guardrails.
  • Attackers break harmful requests into harmless sub-queries.
  • An adaptive agent uses model responses to build a harmful answer.
  • This bypasses single-prompt safety checks effectively.
  • The attack works on major commercial models with over 95% success.
  • Mitigations require context-aware, multi-turn intent analysis beyond current defenses.
